subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose restart catch-up controls in public cron config, and should the supported shape be the existing global max/stagger knobs, a skip/freshness policy, or no new public config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the choice changes public configuration and scheduler semantics for existing cron jobs after restart.

options.title: Expose narrow global controls
options.body: Approve documented global cron restart catch-up controls based on the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit zero-limit semantics if maintainers want disable support.

options.title: Design a skip policy first
options.body: Prefer a global or per-job skip/freshness policy before exposing knobs, preserving current catch-up defaults for existing users until the policy is settled.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Decline new public config and document the current fixed restart catch-up behavior and safer job patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Expose narrow global controls
recommendation.body: Approve documented global cron restart catch-up controls based on the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit zero-limit semantics if maintainers want disable support.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public config and scheduler-semantics decision, and steipete merged the original restart catch-up behavior plus appears in adjacent cron/config history.
